delta_findings.finding: Current remote adds observer.disconnect() to listenersToRemove. removeListeners() runs those callbacks. The snapshot's missing-disconnect observation must not be reported as a current remote gap.

Current remote adds resizeCleanupRef and unmount cleanup, cleans the previous gesture registration before a new one, registers pointerup on activeCell.elem.ownerDocument, and removes that registration after a successful commit. Portal target uses editor root's ownerDocument.body with global document.body fallback. The snapshot's missing unmount cleanup/global-document-only finding is superseded.

Current remote still mounts one TableCellResizer per playground Editor and conditionally renders exactly two physical right/bottom handles for the one active cell. No per-cell map or first-column left handle was introduced. Diff leaves hit-testing, size defaults, guide preview and dimension commits unchanged; pointerup still invokes row-height/column-width update then reset.
delta_findings.limit: Source ownership/cardinality only; no rendering-cost, performance or browser interaction claim.

delta_findings.finding: The remote resizer delta introduces no keyboard/Escape, RTL logical-edge, pointercancel, blur or lost-pointer-capture handler. It retains editable-only portal rendering. Those absence statements are bounded to the fully read snapshot file plus its complete remote diff. Unmount listener cleanup is present now; do not conflate that improvement with an explicit cancel/rollback gesture policy.

Separately from resizing, current table-selection dragging tracks pointerId, pointerStartCell and isPointerDrag, uses a 10px tap-slop box, defers touch anchoring until a drag crosses cells, and stops on matching pointercancel or lostpointercapture. Touch drags may auto-scroll after becoming drags. These policies belong to the table browser helper/observer, not the resizer.
delta_findings.limit: No touch-device/native parity claim; changed tests were not evaluated.

delta_findings.finding: Deleting all selected rows now selects before the table before removing it. Partial clear copies an existing paragraph, retaining presentation while emptying children. Utility delta also preserves presentation when unmerging, resets positional span/width/header state on split cells, avoids an extra empty paragraph during merge, and copies vertical alignment during structured-table paste. These remain table-feature semantics; $clearText still lives on TableObserver.
delta_findings.limit: The snapshot's conditional invalid-selection regression test is historical evidence, not proof of the current all-row deletion path.

delta_findings.finding: Current table helpers reuse the expanded rectangle for formatting, replace the merged-anchor-corner throw with a fallback corner policy, restrict the ArrowDown deferred workaround to selections before the table, and refine Firefox shift-click behavior around nested tables. The split between model topology and browser input/geometry remains.

TableSelection and React TablePlugin are whole-file identical. TableExtension's delta only removes PURE comments. registerTablePlugin's delta adds row-header inheritance when padding rows. No change moves table semantics into React or core in these inspected deltas.

TableNode and TableRowNode replace handwritten JSON/clone methods with nodeSchema/generated declarations; the schemas retain table-owned colWidths and row-owned height, and the setters remain. Table DOM export/import additionally carries direction. EditorState adds compact JSON plumbing while retaining a root-only JSON result and BaseSelection state slot.
delta_findings.limit: Generated serialization machinery outside these files was not audited. This is not a full current public API, serialization compatibility or RTL-resize claim.

findings.finding: TableSelection implements core BaseSelection and occupies EditorState._selection. It stores tableKey and anchor/focus PointType keys, clones points, never reports collapsed, and caches selected descendants. Selection is therefore not merely React/UI state.
findings.limit: This supports a generic selection protocol with optional feature semantics; it does not justify putting table-specific nodes or algorithms in editor core.

findings.finding: The model map repeats a cell value across rowspan/colspan coverage, with startRow/startColumn. Rectangle expansion includes whole intersecting merged cells and selection traversal deduplicates by key. Separately getTable() indexes encountered DOM cells and attaches _cell records; TableNode exposes DOM-coordinate lookup methods. These are distinct projections with different semantics.
findings.limit: The getNodes() caching TODO is not measurement or proof that a persistent incremental map is warranted.

findings.finding: There is no mapping method in BaseSelection. TableSelection.isValid() guards root/type/existence and getNodes() returns [] for invalid keys. Row deletion explicitly selects a surviving cell; paste merge work selects a cell from a recomputed map. Cross-cell RangeSelection conversion and table-exit conversion use the observer/browser path.
findings.limit: Do not infer complete edit/CRDT remapping from key-based addressing. The deleted-row regression test conditionally checks invalid selection if a TableSelection remains; it does not prove preservation of the selected rectangle.

findings.finding: Generic clipboard code accepts BaseSelection and delegates insertion through SELECTION_INSERT_CLIPBOARD_NODES_COMMAND. TableSelection outputs tab/newline cell text; raw text builds a temporary TSV table and pastes through a RangeSelection at the anchor, allowing growth. A structured table pasted onto TableSelection is clipped to the expanded selection boundary; affected merged cells are unmerged and template spans reconstructed. Partial-table HTML export has a test preserving the selected column's width. Document paste/copy forwarding compensates for browser event delivery when custom selection lacks a native range.
findings.limit: TSV paste and structured-table paste do not have identical clipping semantics. The observer comment about native-menu copying is not treated as a current blanket failure: the later document-level copy handler and its unit test must also be considered.

findings.finding: TableObserver stores DOM elements, gesture state and a TableSelection mirror, but also implements $formatCells and $clearText. Partial clear replaces cell contents with empty paragraphs; a first/last-cell whole-table check removes the table and inserts a paragraph if root becomes empty. Delete/cut commands invoke these observer methods, so semantic deletion is attached to the DOM observer lifecycle.
findings.inference: A transferable ownership cut is to make formatting/clearing model operations callable without constructing a TableObserver, with the browser adapter invoking them and repainting.

findings.finding: The DOM observer installs high-priority arrows, Escape, delete and optional Tab handlers. Tab follows real cell siblings/rows and exits the table at its ends. Vertical arrow handling measures caret/cell-edge rectangles; Shift+arrow on TableSelection uses the span-aware model map; Escape selects the focus cell's end. Typeahead can retain vertical arrows.
findings.inference: Keep logical cell targeting in the optional table feature and geometry/event arbitration in its browser adapter; moving every key policy to core would not eliminate the layout dependency.

findings.finding: The selection registration owns a TableObservers registry. Mutation listeners create observers, replace them when table DOM identity changes, and remove them on destruction; unregister removes all. Window pointerdown uses registerRootListener because extension registration can precede root mounting. Registry sweeps prune missing table keys. Pointerup/buttons-up stops drag listeners and auto-scroll; observers use AbortController for event listeners.
findings.limit: In the inspected TableObserver.trackTable() body, MutationObserver is a local variable with observe() but no recorded disconnect in removeListeners(). This is a source-level lifetime gap, not a reproduced leak or crash.

findings.finding: The playground resizer tracks pointer start, active DOM cell, direction and current pointer in React refs/state. Pointer moves update the guide-line position, not row/column dimensions. Pointerup computes a zoom-adjusted delta and performs one editor.update through setColWidths or setHeight, tagged only SKIP_SCROLL_INTO_VIEW_TAG. Persistent widths/heights serialize on table/row nodes.
findings.limit: No explicit history boundary/grouping policy or collaboration conflict policy appears in the resize commit path. The mounting transform also writes default widths. Source supports preview/commit separation, not a guarantee of exactly one undo item.

findings.finding: Upstream has one resizer overlay per mounted playground Editor, showing handles for one active cell. Editor renders a single TableCellResizer component; the plugin portals one TableCellResizer into document.body. Its JSX conditionally renders exactly two handle divs when activeCell is non-null: physical right and bottom. There is no per-cell handle mapping, per-table overlay instance, or first-column left handle in this implementation.
findings.hit_testing: Root pointermove finds the target TD/TH through getDOMCellFromTarget, which walks DOM ancestors and returns the _cell record created by the table DOM observer. Root pointerdown also runs that path for touch. Pointer movement within the resizer container is ignored when not dragging; during drag it updates pointerCurrentPos. Handle layout reads active-cell and table bounding rectangles. A 16px hit zone straddles each right/bottom edge; during drag the active handle becomes a 3px guide spanning the table. CSS positions the handles absolutely and sets touch-action:none.

observed_input_policies.keyboard: Handle JSX registers pointer handlers only and supplies no tabIndex, role or keyboard handler. Full resizer TSX/CSS inspection and a bounded key/Escape search found no resize-keyboard implementation here. This does not claim editor-wide keyboard absence.
observed_input_policies.rtl: Direction is the physical union 'right' | 'bottom'; right-handle placement uses left + width and width commit uses clientX delta. No RTL/direction lookup or logical-edge flip appears in this resizer. No RTL runtime claim.
observed_input_policies.cancel: Pointerup commits and resets. No pointercancel, Escape, lost-pointer-capture or blur cancellation path appears in the complete resizer file. The per-drag document pointerup listener is removed within the successful commit path, without a matching unmount cleanup in this file.
observed_input_policies.read_only: TableCellResizerPlugin reads useLexicalEditable and renders the portal only when true. This gates the resizer component, its default-width transform and its effect registrations. A transition during an active drag is not explicitly handled by the per-drag pointerup lifetime.

findings.comparison_boundary: User reports local TableCellResizeControls renders bottom/right handles in every cell plus a left handle in the first column and table-owned shared preview. Local code was not inspected by this worker; the lead owns that comparison. Upstream source supplies the editor-scoped active-cell overlay counterexample, with no rendering-cost, timing or browser-proof claim.

findings.finding: The resizer exists only while editable, renders through a portal into global document.body, and cleans up mutation/root listeners via effects. Drag start adds a document pointerup handler; that handler removes itself after successful commit/reset. The complete inspected file supplies no pointercancel/Escape handler or effect cleanup for that per-drag pointerup registration, and commit resolves a retained active DOM cell.
findings.limit: Do not promote the playground drag controller unchanged. Interrupted drag, deleted cell, unmount, root/document replacement and stale DOM are policy gaps to assess; none was reproduced here.

findings.finding: TableNode initializes __colWidths as an own property, and Yjs node-property discovery enumerates own properties of a constructed node. Cursor-awareness sync creates relative positions only for RangeSelection; TableSelection is not mapped to those positions in this path. Table tests can run in collab V1/V2 modes and assert both editor frames, while local selection coordinates are read from the left frame.
findings.limit: This is evidence for separate document, awareness, and local gesture ownership. It is not proof of remote cell-selection display, concurrent structural-edit correctness, resize conflict behavior, or an executed collaboration pass.

strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.kind: External-source inference for lead assessment; not a local Plite/Plate verdict
strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.promotion: Use a generic core selection protocol to make optional table selection usable by shared editor/clipboard operations; retain table topology, spans, selected-cell enumeration and structural operations in one optional table semantic owner.
strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.cut: Remove semantic formatting/clearing ownership from the DOM observer and remove DOM-coordinate addressing from the table model API when defining a cleaner target. Keep the observer as a browser projection/input adapter; keep resize preview and visual handles local, committing only dimensions through the table semantic owner.
strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.counterargument: Lexical's table package already shares one implementation across React and extension consumers. Browser geometry, native selection conversion and event ordering are real requirements, and a thin adapter alone cannot replace them. A generic selection protocol also does not automatically provide correct mapping, remote selection awareness or every editing operation: TableSelection.insertText() is a no-op. Splitting into extra public packages/controllers without another current consumer could add cost without removing ownership overlap.
strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.adoption_limit: Do not copy Lexical's broad API, mutation caches or optionality boundaries wholesale. The lead must compare local jobs and hard laws before retaining/promoting any abstraction.
strongest_supported_promotion_or_cut.resize_cardinality_implication: One editor-scoped active-cell overlay is an evidenced alternative to mounting handles for every cell. Retain semantic table ownership of committed dimensions; handle mounting, DOM hit-testing, guide rendering and gesture lifetime can be shared by the view. This is a source-backed design candidate, not a measured performance win or local verdict.
